text: 64 clubs in a knockout cup. Pairings are drawn and the club drawn first has the home right; in a tie between a licensed-league club and an amateur club the amateur club is at home. A tie still level after extra time is decided on penalties. The final is played at the Olympiastadion in Berlin, which has hosted it since 1985; the State of Berlin reports an agreement that keeps it there until at least 2030. The length of extra time in the men's cup was not found.

text: Entrants: the Bundesliga and 2. Bundesliga clubs of the previous season (36), the champion and the next three clubs of the previous 3. Liga season (4), and the 21 winners of the regional association cups (Landespokal). The last three places go to the associations with the most teams, at most one extra each, decided by the DFB's Spielausschuss from membership statistics. Second teams of licensed clubs may not enter. If a Landespokal winner is not eligible or already qualified, the next-placed eligible team of that cup takes the place; if a 3. Liga club that qualified through the league wins its Landespokal, the loser of that final moves up. A second source counts the regional places differently (22 cup winners plus named extra places); the difference was not resolved.
basis: Search-result summary of the DFB mode page (which the summary says repeats the same logic for 2026-27) and of a second site; neither page was opened.

text: Two-legged tie between the 16th-placed Bundesliga club and the 3rd-placed 2. Bundesliga club: the aggregate decides, there is no away-goals rule, and extra time and penalties follow if it is level. One top-flight place is at stake. In 2026 the first leg ended 0:0 and Paderborn beat Wolfsburg 2:1 after extra time in the return leg. The two sources agree on the format; the play-offs have been two-legged since 2008/09.

text: Two-legged tie between the 16th-placed 2. Bundesliga club and the 3rd-placed 3. Liga club, decided on aggregate with no away-goals rule, then extra time and penalties. The winner plays in the 2. Bundesliga next season, the loser in the 3. Liga. In 2026 the third-tier club hosted the first leg because its last matchday came a day earlier; Essen won it 1:0 and Fürth won the return 2:0 at home to stay up. text: Not a 3. Liga club against a Regionalliga club: two Regionalliga champions play home and away for the last promotion place to the 3. Liga, while the other promotion places go to champions directly. The sources describe the model as two direct places (West, Südwest), one rotating direct place for Nord, Nordost or Bayern, and a two-legged play-off between the other two champions. A reform vote in June 2026 produced no clear result and the sources put any change at 2028/29 at the earliest, so the current model is expected to apply in 2026/27 - not confirmed by a DFB statement. Which two champions meet is unknown until the Regionalliga seasons end. In 2026 Würzburger Kickers beat Lok Leipzig in this play-off (the sources give the first leg as 1:0 and the second as 2:1 in Würzburg's favour).

text: In 2025-26 the two Superliga clubs just above the directly relegated 15th and 16th places each met one of the top Liga 2 clubs (the third and fourth placed) in a two-legged tie. In 2026 Farul Constanța drew 3-3 and 1-1 with Chindia Târgoviște and stayed up on penalties; FC Voluntari lost 2-3 at Hermannstadt, then won 3-0 at home and went up. Which clubs meet is unknown until the end of the play-out. The 2026-27 competition rules were not found, so the format may change.
